clue.text: Turkey leg Bob demolished? Right!

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and rebuilt differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook takes apart a turkey leg and exclaims in approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' is the anagram signal on 'leg Bob'; 'Turkey' at the front is the bird, capitalised only as the opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobbler is an informal name for a male turkey, after the noise it makes.

clue.text: Point, when American soldier's on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
ST, street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone notes the moment a US soldier sets off down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of an argument is its main point or essence.

clue.text: Top, black, suitable for surfers?

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: A shopper describes a black top as fit for the beach crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfers are web surfers, not wave riders; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A website that is browsable is easy for internet surfers to look through.

clue.text: Volume was illuminating, with accompanying note

parts.note: a lamp that was illuminating a room lit it
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A loud passage lit up the hall, with a musical note in support.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume, a measure of capacity.

clue.text: Communist: the German revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A communist is described as a German revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the traditional political colour and nickname of a communist.

clue.text: Row after catching grand, wild cat

indicators.note: the row catches the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after someone catches a grand prize: a wild one.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger is a large wild member of the cat family.

clue.text: Violinist's last seen on composer's journeys

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece seen on another sits above it
the last letter of the word violinist is taken

parts.note: Ravel was a French composer; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A violinist's final appearance is on a composer's works.
explanation.definitionFit: Travels are journeys, especially long trips abroad.

clue.text: My half of child's horse

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: nursery talk for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone claims a share in a child's toy horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee and my are both mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: Comes back on steamship going round small lake

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: the steamship goes round, enclosing the lake

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
a pond is a small lake

explanation.surface: A steamer circles a little lake and returns to shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to come back with an answer.

clue.text: Ermine Street coming across to Alconbury at first

indicators.note: the street stretches across the other letters, around them
only the first letter of Alconbury is taken

explanation.surface: Directions: Ermine Street crosses over to the village of Alconbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermine Street is a Roman road north from London, passing near Alconbury in Cambridgeshire; here 'Ermine' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat, so the two name one animal.

clue.text: Artist's pants

definitions.meaning: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: The painter's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers is an old word for underwear, and a drawer is someone who sketches.

clue.text: Gather idiot has badge with end missing

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an emblem is a badge or symbol

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers around a fool wearing a broken badge.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to come together or collect in one place.

clue.text: Bottom of ship's bunk

definitions.meaning: the lowest inner part of a ship's hull
bunk, short for bunkum, is nonsense

explanation.surface: A sailor's bed sits in the lowest part of the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a sailor's bed but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is the ship's bottom and also slang for worthless talk.

clue.text: Overheard couple too much

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper finds a pair excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'too much' runs together; 'much', as in 'a bit much', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive, overly so.

clue.text: Tango with novel footwear in song from musical

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer pairs the tango with new shoes for a show number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is the anagram signal on 'footwear'; the song comes from the 1925 musical No, No, Nanette.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea for Two is the famous song from the 1925 musical No, No, Nanette.

clue.text: Oust violently with veto to achieve defeats democratically

indicators.note: violent treatment tears the letters apart and throws them together again

explanation.surface: Violently ousting and vetoing is contrasted with winning by ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To outvote people is to beat them by a majority in a vote.

clue.text: Bald Ulsterman moved item of hall furniture?

indicators.note: letters moved around take up a new order

explanation.surface: A hairless man from Northern Ireland is shifted like a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella stand is a holder for brollies, typically kept in an entrance hall.

clue.text: Rubbish solution for irritated viewers

definitions.meaning: a liquid solution for bathing sore eyes, the viewers

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a remedy for sore eyes as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is lotion for the eyes, and figuratively humbug or claptrap.

clue.text: Struggle avoided, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are skipped, so only the even ones are kept

explanation.surface: A fight was dodged, defying the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or strive against rivals.

clue.text: Celeb briefly backed into corrupt poll

indicators.note: backed means the shortened word is read backwards
said briefly, the word loses its last letter
corrupt letters are spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: A celebrity briefly backs a corrupt ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts Celeb to CELE, 'backed' turns it to ELEC, and 'corrupt' turns INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An election is a poll, a vote to choose representatives.

clue.text: Part of flower — and of date palm

indicators.note: and of carries over 'part of', so a part of the phrase that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A petal-like bit belongs to a flower and a palm tree too.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Part of' of the definition carries over: 'and of date palm' means and also part of the words date palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepal is a floral segment where petals and sepals cannot be told apart.

clue.text: Daughter's head: strange place to do tattoo

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A parent finds the daughter's head an odd site for a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The tattoo is a drumbeat, as in a military tattoo, not ink on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic beating, performed on a drum.

clue.text: Those people must accept rebuke for this treatment

indicators.note: the word takes in, accepting the rebuke inside it

parts.note: they means those people
a rap is a sharp rebuke

explanation.surface: Patients must accept criticism as part of their therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment for an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Old priest: the Spanish one

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly priest is pointed out as the Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

clue.text: Yours truly's up for eating a potato

indicators.note: the reversed word eats the letter, holding it inside
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: yours truly means me, so its possessive is my

explanation.surface: Someone's turn comes up to eat a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is called a sweet potato in the US, a starchy tuber.

clue.text: Boy trapped back in concrete pillar

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
trapped in says the answer is held inside the words that follow
in, with trapped, says the answer is held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boy is stuck inside a concrete pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Boy trapped' was wrong: 'Boy' alone defines, and 'trapped ... in' signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is a common English male first name, so it fits a boy by example.

clue.text: Forger sends money in two holdalls first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter sends cash split between two bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter but means one who forges metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith works metal at a forge, shaping it by hammering.

clue.text: Chap's local refurbished in 2000

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so 2000 is MM

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's pub was done up at the millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' turns LOCAL into ALCOL; a local is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm is a man's name, so a chap.
